subject.title: Cron run drops a produced deliverable when an ancillary backgrounded tool exits non-zero

question: What should the durable isolated cron terminal-status contract do when final assistant output exists but a background/tool process exits non-zero?
rationale: Current code has multiple plausible signals: final assistant text, tool error payloads, run-level errors, failure signals, diagnostics, and delivery state; choosing which one wins can change alerts, failure counters, and message delivery.

options.title: Structured Recovery Contract
options.body: Treat explicit non-terminal background/tool failures as warning diagnostics when final output is valid, while keeping typed run-level/fatal signals authoritative.

options.title: Broad Final Text Recovery
options.body: Let final assistant-visible text recover most non-fatal tool payload errors, accepting the risk that some real terminal tool failures may be marked ok.

options.title: Strict Failure Option First
options.body: Keep current conservative defaults and add or revive an opt-in fail-on-tool-failure/status contract before changing default recovery semantics.

recommendation.title: Structured Recovery Contract
recommendation.body: Treat explicit non-terminal background/tool failures as warning diagnostics when final output is valid, while keeping typed run-level/fatal signals authoritative.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on cron final-output and error-status semantics in the affected helper/finalization path.
